purpose: Independently test whether FRC-RAG evidence selection preserves distinct, naturally occurring conflicting answer viewpoints under a fixed context budget better than five reproducible selectors on the previously untouched WhoQA benchmark.

frozen_source.paper: Who's Who: Large Language Models Meet Knowledge Conflicts in Practice

frozen_task.unit: one WhoQA question with all provided supporting contexts as candidate evidence
frozen_task.candidate: one supporting context associated with one same-name entity
frozen_task.candidate_text: the public supporting context exactly as distributed, with no gold answer metadata appended
frozen_task.gold_viewpoint: the public answer set associated with the candidate entity
frozen_task.gold_visibility: answer sets and entity-to-answer mapping are isolated from scoring and selection and are read only by the evaluator
frozen_task.duplicate_viewpoint_rule: answer sets are canonicalized as sorted case-folded strings; contexts with identical canonical answer sets belong to the same viewpoint
frozen_task.empty_answer_rule: cases with missing question, contexts, or answer alignment fail validation rather than being silently dropped
frozen_task.sampling: all official evaluation questions; no sampling and no fitting

role_queries.answer_claim: Find evidence that directly states an answer to the question.
role_queries.entity_attribution: Find evidence that identifies which specific same-name entity, source, role, place, or time the answer belongs to.
role_queries.alternative_claim: Find evidence that may support an alternative answer or interpretation of the question.
role_queries.ambiguity_disclosure: Find evidence useful for disclosing that the question can refer to multiple different same-name entities.

frozen_selection.tie_break: candidate id ascending after the frozen selector-specific score ordering

primary.name: oracle_normalized_distinct_viewpoint_coverage
primary.definition: selected distinct gold viewpoints divided by min(total distinct gold viewpoints, the maximum number of candidates selectable under Top-K and token budget)

secondary: complete viewpoint disclosure rate for cases with at most four viewpoints
strata: each public property type with at least 50 cases
frozen_metrics.strongest_baseline_comparison: For each bootstrap resample, subtract the maximum aggregate primary score among all five baselines from the FRC aggregate score; percentile bounds are therefore simultaneous with data-dependent strongest-baseline selection.
frozen_metrics.reference_baseline_comparison: Paired FRC minus coverage_greedy_proxy case-level primary difference with the same frozen bootstrap seed.

frozen_decision_policy.interpretation_boundary: A positive result supports the evidence-selection mechanism on same-name multi-viewpoint conflicts only. It does not confirm the v32 classifier router, reproduce SetR, establish flood-domain effectiveness, or authorize Gate 2, CANARY, or DEFAULT.
frozen_decision_policy.gate_2: NO-GO/SHADOW regardless of this standalone result

known_limitations: WhoQA conflicts arise from same-name entity ambiguity and do not cover temporal invalidation, misinformation, missing files, or flood-domain policy exceptions.
The official candidate contexts are curated supporting evidence rather than a noisy open-corpus retrieval pool.
Gold viewpoint labels evaluate selected contexts but cannot be used to score or select them.
The frozen Top-K=4 budget creates an intentional coverage ceiling for questions with five to eight viewpoints; the primary metric normalizes only against the attainable ceiling.
The experiment evaluates evidence selection, not final natural-language conflict disclosure quality.
